questions.cardText:
[Chemistry] If you let hot liquid bismuth cool off, what will happen to its volume?
A. It will expand
B. It will expand and then contract
C. It will contract
Answer: A. Unlike most metals, bismuth expands as it solidifies, similar to water expands when freezing. This unique property makes it useful in casting applications where precise molds are needed.
questions.en: Unlike most metals, what happens to the volume of liquid bismuth as it cools and solidifies?
questions.de: Was geschieht – anders als bei den meisten Metallen – mit dem Volumen von flüssigem Bismut, wenn es abkühlt und erstarrt?

timeline.labelEn: Claude François Geoffroy shows that bismuth is a metal distinct from lead and tin
timeline.labelDe: Claude François Geoffroy zeigt, dass Bismut ein eigenes Metall ist, verschieden von Blei und Zinn

questions.notes: Card answer confirmed: bismuth expands by 3.32% on solidification (Wikipedia), which is why it was used in low-melting typesetting alloys.

questions.cardText:
[Engineering and Inventions] Which ancient civilization is known to first use concrete extensively in construction?
A. Egyptians B. Greeks C. Romans
Answer: C. The Romans were the first to use concrete extensively, including the Pantheon and the Colosseum. They used a mixture of lime, volcanic ash, and seawater, which allowed the concrete to set underwater and self-heal over time.
questions.en: Which ancient civilization was the first to use concrete extensively in construction, for example in the Pantheon and the Colosseum?
questions.de: Welche antike Zivilisation setzte als erste Beton in großem Umfang im Bauwesen ein, etwa beim Pantheon und beim Kolosseum?

timeline.labelEn: Roman concrete (opus caementicium) comes into widespread use, about 150 BC
timeline.labelDe: Römischer Beton (Opus caementicium) ist ab etwa 150 v. Chr. weit verbreitet

questions.notes: Answer confirmed (Roman concrete in widespread use from about 150 BC; the Pantheon dome is the largest unreinforced concrete dome). The card's explanation oversimplifies: seawater was a factor only in Roman marine concrete, and 2023 research attributes the self-healing to lime clasts in the mix.
